To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a set of cross faults in the Taconics, which are parallel to the paleo-trench and which were active during thrusting, were reactivated during thrusting, (2) the cross faults are the result of flexural loading of the foreland by the accretion of the Taconic allochthon, (3) the cross faults were originally synconvergence normal fault zones that developed in response to flexural loading of an outboard-facing forearc, and

the Taconic thrust system is a composite thrust sheet, with cross faults that are normal faults that developed in response to flexural forebulging of the Laurentian margin during the Taconic orogeny, and that these cross faults are responsible for the observed structural and stratigraphic relationships within the thrust sheet.
